summary: spawn-budget scan silently drops a spawn site when a same-named function is declared elsewhere in the file
acceptance: a case calling a file-local spawn wrapper is still flagged when an unrelated same-named function exists elsewhere in the file
tests: a same-named function elsewhere in the file does not hide a spawning case from the scan
notes: namedFunctions is a Map<string,Node>, so Map.set last-wins collapses shadowed declarations; the surviving node decides reach for the whole file. Measured this tick: a file-local `boot` reaching process.execPath plus a later unrelated `const boot` in a sibling describe scans to []. That is under-approximation, the opposite of the posture the module's doc comment declares. Widen, never scope-bound.
